name: compozy
description: An operating system for AI agents. Plug in the agent CLIs you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) and they become a team: they split the work, hand tasks to each other, run automated on jobs and loops, and share one project memory. You steer everything from the browser.
readmeExcerpt:
CompozyOS

The system around the agent, already built.

An operating system for AI agents.

Anyone can prompt an agent. Making agents work continuously is still an engineering project: loops, triggers, cron, permissions, approvals, observability, and the glue scripts that hold them together. CompozyOS turns that entire agent stack into one product, a complete environment to create, automate, and supervise agent work with the agent CLIs you already use (Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor). Built first for developers and technical operators. > [!NOTE] > v0.4.0 is the first stable CompozyOS release. The previous v0.2 product has reached end of life > and receives no further releases. Start with the [migration guide](MIGRATION_GUIDE.md) before > replacing an existing v0.2 installation.
## ✨ Highlights - **Create.** Sessions, agents, Loops, and capabilities are objects you author once and reuse, not scripts you rewrite per run. - **Automate.** Cron schedules, webhooks, and triggers keep work running with no terminal open. - **Supervise.** Approvals, permissions, run state, artifacts, and agent activity stay inspectable while work continues in the background. - **Work survives the terminal.** Sessions and Loop runs belong to the daemon, so closing one client does not erase the work. - **Runs the agents you already use.** ACP-compatible CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor) operate the same daemon-owned state. - **Batteries included.** One runtime, one state model: loops and approvals are core objects, not plugins, reachable from web, CLI, HTTP/SSE, UDS, MCP, and native tools. - **Local-first by default.** One Go binary and SQLite-backed stores keep runtime state on the operator's machine unless a configured provider or extension owns an external boundary. - **Remote access stays explicit.** The [Gateway](https://compozy.com/docs/gateway) pairs devices and exposes only the private or public surfaces an operator enables. - **Built to extend.** Agents, skills, capabilities, hooks, and extension kits plug into explicit runtime contracts. ## 📦 Installation #### Verified installer The installer pins the latest published release and verifies Sigstore provenance before installing the binary on macOS or Linux. ```bash curl -fsSL https://compozy.com/install.sh | sh ``` #### Homebrew ```bash brew install compozy/compozy/compozy ``` #### NPM ```bash npm install -g @compozy/cli ``` #### Go Install with the explicit tag shown on the [latest release](https://github.com/compozy/compozy/releases/latest): ```bash go install github.com/compozy/compozy@ ``` #### From Source ```bash git clone https://github.com/compozy/compozy.git cd compozy go build -o ./bin/compozy . ``` The [installation guide](https://compozy.com/docs/getting-started/installation) covers installer flags, Linux packages, source builds, verification, and managed updates. ## 🔄 How It Works
People and agents send commands through public control surfaces. The home-scoped daemon resolves the workspace, applies permissions and runtime policy, coordinates ACP agents, and persists events and resource state. Web and streaming clients read that same daemon-owned truth instead of maintaining a parallel model. ### Daemon Runtime Model `compozy daemon start`, `compozy status`, and `compozy daemon stop` manage the local daemon. Sessions, tasks, Loop runs, automation and tools keep explicit owners and workspace boundaries. Use structured CLI output (`-o json`), HTTP/SSE, UDS, MCP, or native tools when another agent or program needs to manage the same resources. ### Task Schema v2 Authored task files remain portable Markdown with typed frontmatter. The v0.3 runtime imports them into durable tasks and executes them through Loops; it does not revive the v0.2 `tasks run` pipeline. See [Migrate from v0.2.15](MIGRATION_GUIDE.md) for the exact schema and command changes. ## ⚙️ Config Files Global defaults live in `~/.compozy/config.toml`; a workspace can override supported fields through `.compozy/config.toml`. Explicit command flags win over workspace configuration, which wins over global configuration and built-in defaults. ```bash compozy config path compozy config validate compozy config show -o json ``` Configuration, credentials, and provider-home policies have different owners. Follow the [configuration guide](https://compozy.com/docs/configuration/config-toml) instead of copying v0.2 state into a v0.3 home. ## Reusable Agents Agent definitions live under `~/.compozy/agents//` or `.compozy/agents//`. Each definition has an `AGENT.md` and may include an agent-local `mcp.json`. Workspace definitions override global definitions as a whole. ```bash compozy agent list -o json compozy agent info general -o json compozy session new --agent general ``` ## 🔌 Extensions Extensions add versioned resources and runtime behavior through declared provide surfaces. The daemon owns discovery, enablement, trust decisions, lifecycle, and hooks; extensions do not bypass public runtime contracts. ### Build one in three commands ```bash compozy extension init hello --template tool-provider-go compozy extension dev hello compozy tool invoke ext__hello__search --workspace . --input '{"query":"compozy"}' ``` Executable extensions are code-first: declare the tool once in code and `compozy extension build` generates the manifest. Resource-only extensions can instead hand-write `extension.toml` and use the same build, dev, reload, and watch loop without running extension code. Walkthrough: [Build your first extension](https://compozy.com/docs/guides/build-your-first-extension). ### SDK support `@compozy/extension-sdk` (npm, MIT) and `github.com/compozy/compozy/sdk/go` are published and version-matched to the daemon. ### Extension CLI ```bash compozy extension list -o json compozy extension status -o json compozy extension provenance -o json compozy extension logs --follow ``` ### Learn more - [Build your first extension](https://compozy.com/docs/guides/build-your-first-extension) - [Extensions](https://compozy.com/docs/extensions) - [Publish an extension](https://compozy.com/docs/extensions/publish) - [Capabilities and extension kits](https://compozy.com/docs/extensions) - [Official CompozyOS skill](skills/compozy/) - [Migration guide](MIGRATION_GUIDE.md) ## Build an app Use `@compozy/client` for TypeScript or `github.com/compozy/compozy/sdk/go/client` for Go to connect an external app to your running daemon. Both clients provide typed operations and agent streams; app tokens authorize trusted browser origins on the local listener. Follow the [Build an app tutorials](https://compozy.com/docs/apps) for Node, a server-backed chat UI, browser access, Go, and token administration. The [API reference](https://compozy.com/docs/api) includes generated SDK calls for each operation. These app SDK surfaces are experimental in 0.4; pin the exact version matching your daemon. ## 🚀 Quick Start Bootstrap the home, start the daemon, enter the repository you want agents to work in, and create one durable session. CompozyOS infers and registers the workspace from the current directory; use `--workspace ` only when you need an override. ```bash compozy install compozy daemon start compozy session new --agent general --name first-run ``` The [Quick Start](https://compozy.com/docs/getting-started/quick-start) continues through the first prompt, live attachment, inspection, and cleanup. ## 🧩 Skills Skills are daemon-discovered resources with explicit source and scope. Use the structured skill and marketplace surfaces to inspect what is active instead of copying v0.2 setup directories forward. ```bash compozy skill list -o json compozy skill inspect -o json compozy marketplace search --kind skill --query -o json ``` ### 🧠 Workflow Memory Workflow memory is ordinary repository files under `.compozy/tasks//memory/`, written and read by the spec-cycle skills. The v0.2 workflow-memory files remain repository artifacts; they are not imported as hidden runtime state. ### 🤖 Supported Agents CompozyOS runs ACP-compatible agent CLIs and adapters. The active provider catalog and each agent's runtime settings are runtime truth; inspect them before selecting a model or reasoning mode. See the [provider guide](https://compozy.com/docs/agents/providers) for authentication and provider-home policies. ## 📖 CLI Reference The generated [CLI reference](https://compozy.com/docs/cli-reference) is authoritative for verbs, flags, structured output, and exit behavior. Start with: ```bash compozy --help compozy version compozy doctor -o json ``` ## Documentation - [Runtime overview](https://compozy.com/docs) - [Installation](https://compozy.com/docs/getting-started/installation) - [Quick Start](https://compozy.com/docs/getting-started/quick-start) - [Migrate from v0.2.15](MIGRATION_GUIDE.md) - [CLI reference](https://compozy.com/docs/cli-reference) - [GitHub releases](https://github.com/compozy/compozy/releases) ## 🛠️ Development CompozyOS is a Go and Bun monorepo. Start the daemon with automatic Go rebuilds and the web UI with Vite HMR: ```bash make dev ``` To populate the Northstar Pay demo and leave its daemon running in the background: ```bash make demo-seed # Optional isolated home and secondary port: make demo-seed DEMO_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo-other" DEMO_PORT=2125 ``` This builds the daemon and Web bundle, replaces the seed-owned scenario, and starts the demo at `http://localhost:2124` using `~/.compozy-demo` by default. The main instance is unchanged. To reseed a running demo, first stop its daemon with `COMPOZY_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo" ./bin/compozy daemon stop` (use your custom home if overridden). The raw `go run ./scripts/demo-seed --home ` command remains available for data-only seeding. Existing demos in `~/.agh` can still be selected explicitly with `DEMO_HOME`. To prepare the same demo and open it in the Electron desktop shell: ```bash make demo-seed-desktop # The same overrides apply: make demo-seed-desktop DEMO_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo-other" DEMO_PORT=2125 ``` The desktop shell uses the demo home for its runtime connection and Electron profile. Quitting Electron leaves the demo daemon running in the background. As with `demo-seed`, stop an already-running demo before reseeding it. Run the affected local gate before committing or pushing: ```bash make gate ``` Delivery finishes in the draft PR: wait for every required CI check to pass on its current head. Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the surface-specific instructions before editing. ## Star History
readmeHtml:
CompozyOS

The system around the agent, already built.

An operating system for AI agents.

Anyone can prompt an agent. Making agents work continuously is still an engineering project: loops, triggers, cron, permissions, approvals, observability, and the glue scripts that hold them together. CompozyOS turns that entire agent stack into one product, a complete environment to create, automate, and supervise agent work with the agent CLIs you already use (Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor). Built first for developers and technical operators.

Note

v0.4.0 is the first stable CompozyOS release. The previous v0.2 product has reached end of life and receives no further releases. Start with the migration guide before replacing an existing v0.2 installation.

✨ Highlights

  • Create. Sessions, agents, Loops, and capabilities are objects you author once and reuse, not scripts you rewrite per run.
  • Automate. Cron schedules, webhooks, and triggers keep work running with no terminal open.
  • Supervise. Approvals, permissions, run state, artifacts, and agent activity stay inspectable while work continues in the background.
  • Work survives the terminal. Sessions and Loop runs belong to the daemon, so closing one client does not erase the work.
  • Runs the agents you already use. ACP-compatible CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor) operate the same daemon-owned state.
  • Batteries included. One runtime, one state model: loops and approvals are core objects, not plugins, reachable from web, CLI, HTTP/SSE, UDS, MCP, and native tools.
  • Local-first by default. One Go binary and SQLite-backed stores keep runtime state on the operator's machine unless a configured provider or extension owns an external boundary.
  • Remote access stays explicit. The Gateway pairs devices and exposes only the private or public surfaces an operator enables.
  • Built to extend. Agents, skills, capabilities, hooks, and extension kits plug into explicit runtime contracts.

📦 Installation

Verified installer

The installer pins the latest published release and verifies Sigstore provenance before installing the binary on macOS or Linux.

curl -fsSL https://compozy.com/install.sh | sh

Homebrew

brew install compozy/compozy/compozy

NPM

npm install -g @compozy/cli

Go

Install with the explicit tag shown on the latest release:

go install github.com/compozy/compozy@<release-tag>

From Source

git clone https://github.com/compozy/compozy.git
cd compozy
go build -o ./bin/compozy .

The installation guide covers installer flags, Linux packages, source builds, verification, and managed updates.

🔄 How It Works

People and agents send commands through public control surfaces. The home-scoped daemon resolves the workspace, applies permissions and runtime policy, coordinates ACP agents, and persists events and resource state. Web and streaming clients read that same daemon-owned truth instead of maintaining a parallel model.

Daemon Runtime Model

compozy daemon start, compozy status, and compozy daemon stop manage the local daemon. Sessions, tasks, Loop runs, automation and tools keep explicit owners and workspace boundaries. Use structured CLI output (-o json), HTTP/SSE, UDS, MCP, or native tools when another agent or program needs to manage the same resources.

Task Schema v2

Authored task files remain portable Markdown with typed frontmatter. The v0.3 runtime imports them into durable tasks and executes them through Loops; it does not revive the v0.2 tasks run pipeline. See Migrate from v0.2.15 for the exact schema and command changes.

⚙️ Config Files

Global defaults live in ~/.compozy/config.toml; a workspace can override supported fields through .compozy/config.toml. Explicit command flags win over workspace configuration, which wins over global configuration and built-in defaults.

compozy config path
compozy config validate
compozy config show -o json

Configuration, credentials, and provider-home policies have different owners. Follow the configuration guide instead of copying v0.2 state into a v0.3 home.

Reusable Agents

Agent definitions live under ~/.compozy/agents/<name>/ or .compozy/agents/<name>/. Each definition has an AGENT.md and may include an agent-local mcp.json. Workspace definitions override global definitions as a whole.

compozy agent list -o json
compozy agent info general -o json
compozy session new --agent general

🔌 Extensions

Extensions add versioned resources and runtime behavior through declared provide surfaces. The daemon owns discovery, enablement, trust decisions, lifecycle, and hooks; extensions do not bypass public runtime contracts.

Build one in three commands

compozy extension init hello --template tool-provider-go
compozy extension dev hello
compozy tool invoke ext__hello__search --workspace . --input '{"query":"compozy"}'

Executable extensions are code-first: declare the tool once in code and compozy extension build generates the manifest. Resource-only extensions can instead hand-write extension.toml and use the same build, dev, reload, and watch loop without running extension code. Walkthrough: Build your first extension.

SDK support

@compozy/extension-sdk (npm, MIT) and github.com/compozy/compozy/sdk/go are published and version-matched to the daemon.

Extension CLI

compozy extension list -o json
compozy extension status <name> -o json
compozy extension provenance <name> -o json
compozy extension logs <name> --follow

Learn more

  • Build your first extension
  • Extensions
  • Publish an extension
  • Capabilities and extension kits
  • Official CompozyOS skill
  • Migration guide

Build an app

Use @compozy/client for TypeScript or github.com/compozy/compozy/sdk/go/client for Go to connect an external app to your running daemon. Both clients provide typed operations and agent streams; app tokens authorize trusted browser origins on the local listener.

Follow the Build an app tutorials for Node, a server-backed chat UI, browser access, Go, and token administration. The API reference includes generated SDK calls for each operation. These app SDK surfaces are experimental in 0.4; pin the exact version matching your daemon.

🚀 Quick Start

Bootstrap the home, start the daemon, enter the repository you want agents to work in, and create one durable session. CompozyOS infers and registers the workspace from the current directory; use --workspace <id|name|path> only when you need an override.

compozy install
compozy daemon start
compozy session new --agent general --name first-run

The Quick Start continues through the first prompt, live attachment, inspection, and cleanup.

🧩 Skills

Skills are daemon-discovered resources with explicit source and scope. Use the structured skill and marketplace surfaces to inspect what is active instead of copying v0.2 setup directories forward.

compozy skill list -o json
compozy skill inspect <name> -o json
compozy marketplace search --kind skill --query <term> -o json

🧠 Workflow Memory

Workflow memory is ordinary repository files under .compozy/tasks/<name>/memory/, written and read by the spec-cycle skills. The v0.2 workflow-memory files remain repository artifacts; they are not imported as hidden runtime state.

🤖 Supported Agents

CompozyOS runs ACP-compatible agent CLIs and adapters. The active provider catalog and each agent's runtime settings are runtime truth; inspect them before selecting a model or reasoning mode. See the provider guide for authentication and provider-home policies.

📖 CLI Reference

The generated CLI reference is authoritative for verbs, flags, structured output, and exit behavior. Start with:

compozy --help
compozy version
compozy doctor -o json

Documentation

  • Runtime overview
  • Installation
  • Quick Start
  • Migrate from v0.2.15
  • CLI reference
  • GitHub releases

🛠️ Development

CompozyOS is a Go and Bun monorepo. Start the daemon with automatic Go rebuilds and the web UI with Vite HMR:

make dev

To populate the Northstar Pay demo and leave its daemon running in the background:

make demo-seed
# Optional isolated home and secondary port:
make demo-seed DEMO_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo-other" DEMO_PORT=2125

This builds the daemon and Web bundle, replaces the seed-owned scenario, and starts the demo at http://localhost:2124 using ~/.compozy-demo by default. The main instance is unchanged. To reseed a running demo, first stop its daemon with COMPOZY_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo" ./bin/compozy daemon stop (use your custom home if overridden). The raw go run ./scripts/demo-seed --home <path> command remains available for data-only seeding. Existing demos in ~/.agh can still be selected explicitly with DEMO_HOME.

To prepare the same demo and open it in the Electron desktop shell:

make demo-seed-desktop
# The same overrides apply:
make demo-seed-desktop DEMO_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo-other" DEMO_PORT=2125

The desktop shell uses the demo home for its runtime connection and Electron profile. Quitting Electron leaves the demo daemon running in the background. As with demo-seed, stop an already-running demo before reseeding it.

Run the affected local gate before committing or pushing:

make gate

Delivery finishes in the draft PR: wait for every required CI check to pass on its current head.

Read AGENTS.md and the surface-specific instructions before editing.

Star History

🤝 Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Open an issue or pull request, keep public behavior agent-manageable, and run make gate before sending changes, then keep the PR until its current-head CI is green. Security reports belong in the repository's private security channel, not a public issue.

Contributors

Thanks to everyone who has contributed to CompozyOS.

📄 License

CompozyOS is distributed under the MIT License.

releases.name: CompozyOS 0.4.6 — stable
releases.body:
## 0.4.6 - 2026-10-30



### Bug Fixes

- Make automatic titles lightweight and retry failed attempts
- Return conversation clear after durable reset
- Default terminals to the account login shell and open them from a launcher
- Refresh session rows in every catalog scope when the runtime changes
- Stop requests for unavailable desktop resources (#1038)
- Hand focus between project overlays before hiding their origins (#1040)
- Preserve Claude usage access across Keychain token refreshes (#1041)
- Restore project menubar focus after context menu dismissal
- Keep focused skip link out of desktop layout
- Report the enforced spawn budget to agents (#1048)
- Share terminal approvals through attention summary
- Restore workspace focus after worktree creation dialog



### Features

- Simplify the Fork session dialog and always fork into this window
- Selection-aware session context menu and project context menus (#1032)
- Group projects into folders and add session totals footer (#1047)
- Add proto.tsx prototype gallery that renders real web components (#1043)
- Open Kanban sessions in a resizable drawer over the board (#1055)
- Multi-select sessions and run bulk actions on the Kanban

releases.name: CompozyOS 0.4.5 — stable
releases.body:
## 0.4.5 - 2026-10-29



### Bug Fixes

- Preserve default profile customization across daemon startup (#1001)
- Preserve Linux update executor identity across clock drift (#1004)
- Restore terminal lifecycle under All projects and User (#1009)
- Preserve archive recovery and pause rejected automation replacements
- Unblock missing-root recovery and restore native input contracts
- Preserve picker focus and synchronize subagent navigation checks
- Preserve native tool domain errors and sanitized causes (#1014)
- Recover detached message edits after lost acknowledgment (#1018)
- Isolate missing workspace state from healthy operations (#1016)
- Register SQLite Unicode search before opening connections
- Make Goal controls interrupt work and clarify session lifecycle (#1019)
- Expose Compozy native tools in Pi sessions (#1021)



### Features

- Change existing session worktrees in place (#1002)
- Inspect subagents in a resizable activity drawer (#1007)
- Archive projects and add safe removal actions (#1010)



### Performance Improvements

- Accelerate session and app data loading (#1006)



### Testing

- Wait for subagent branch expansion before paging
- Account for uptime in denie

releases.name: CompozyOS 0.4.4 — stable
releases.body:
## 0.4.4 - 2026-10-28



### Bug Fixes

- Preserve active sessions through desktop updates (#991)
- Show truthful subagent status across lists, cards and native tasks (#993)
- Regenerate native tool catalog and approve subagent child_activity schema
- Missing agy acp reasoning effort levels (#858)
- Address subagent status review follow-ups
- Keep the frozen elapsed time on idle subagents
- Split subagent hover preview and expect urgency-ordered branch pages
- Edit session messages directly in the composer (#996)
- Retry refused message edits and keep detached unconfirmed sends



### Features

- Sync Interface and Code fonts across clients (#990)

aiSummary.oneLiner: Local-first operating system connecting disparate AI agent CLIs into a unified collaborative team.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: CompozyOS provides a durable, local runtime environment that effectively connects multiple isolated AI agent CLIs into a highly collaborative project team. It utilizes a robust local daemon to actively manage shared project memory, tasks, permissions, and tool execution across agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. Developers interact with the agents through a sophisticated web shell and CLI, steering the automated jobs and complex loops in real-time. The agents interface dynamically with the system state using structured HTTP, UDS, and native tool surfaces, providing a cohesive workspace that survives terminal closures.
keyFeatures: Agent Orchestration: Seamlessly connects disparate agent CLIs to split tasks, hand off work, and run automated execution loops.
Shared Project Memory: Maintains a single, durable source of context and state that all connected agents can continuously access.
Local Daemon Architecture: Runs entirely locally to securely handle session management, complex permissions, and tool coordination.
Browser-Based Steering: Provides a rich web shell interface for human supervisors to effectively monitor and steer the automated agents.
Standardized Interfaces: Exposes deep system state to agents via structured HTTP, UDS, MCP, and native integrated tools.
Extension Ecosystem: Features a flexible extension architecture allowing developers to build and plug in new tool surfaces effortlessly.

useCases.title: Building Collaborative AI Teams
useCases.description: Plugging in specialized agents for frontend and backend development to work together seamlessly on a single full-stack feature.

useCases.title: Automating Background Workflows
useCases.description: Setting up autonomous agent loops to continuously monitor, review, and fix codebase quality issues running in the background.

useCases.title: Managing Multi-Agent State
useCases.description: Providing a durable, centralized memory store for agents that typically lose valuable context after closing their terminal sessions.

useCases.title: Browser-Supervised Automation
useCases.description: Using the web shell to visually track complex task hand-offs and quickly intervene when agents require specific human feedback.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers and AI researchers looking to orchestrate multiple independent agent CLIs into a highly cohesive, locally managed development team. It is essential for those actively adopting sophisticated multi-agent pipelines.
